title: Who it is for
response: It is made for PC repair shops, IT support techs, freelancers and anyone who reinstalls Windows regularly — including people who do it as a side job or for their own machines. If you touch more than a couple of PCs a month, it pays for itself.
followup: Would you like to see what's included?

title: How people use it
patterns: in practice how does it work
response: Typical run: the machine comes in, you format it and install Windows, plug in the toolkit USB, restore connectivity with the offline drivers, then tick the programs the client needs and start the queue. While it installs, you work on the next machine and come back to a ready PC.
followup: Do you want the checklist version of that?

title: Main benefits
response: Four gains: about an hour reclaimed per machine, drivers that work with no internet, installers that never go stale thanks to the updater, and a predictable setup order that reduces support calls from clients afterwards.
